_comment: Tests Ryde Health node 2c complaint intake (loose, LLM-driven triage redesign, 2026-09-23): confident classification needs no question, genuinely ambiguous complaints get at most one plain-language clarifying question, whole-body/systemic complaints are recognized rather than treated as out of scope, escapes still work, and STEP 7's fallback chain (due-rank order, no more DOC 2 focus-match reorder) still behaves correctly including for a single named practitioner. asap-default tag (added 2026-09-23, call review): STEP 4 no longer asks a standalone timeframe/soon question at all -- it defaults silently to ASAP and always speaks a short complaint-specific modality explanation instead, even for the most common/'obvious' complaints (back/knee/shoulder pain), which the old STEP 4 explicitly skipped.

scenarios.name: Ambiguous MSK complaint gets at most one plain-language clarifying question, never a modality list

history.content: I've been getting really bad lower back pain, it's been going on for about two months

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent's response either (a) asks exactly one clarifying question in plain language describing what two approaches feel like (e.g. hands-on/manual work vs. a rehab-and-exercise approach) without naming clinical modality terms like 'chiropractic' or 'physiotherapy' as a multiple-choice menu, and asks nothing else this turn (no tool call), or (b) if it judges the complaint confidently, moves straight on without asking a clarifying question at all. FAIL if the agent recites the six-category service menu unprompted, asks more than one clarifying question this turn, names clinical modality terms as multiple-choice options, or calls any tool before the complaint has been reasoned about.

scenarios.name: Whole-body/systemic complaint is recognized, not treated as out of scope

history.content: I've just been feeling really run down and achy all over, like my whole body is stiff

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent treats this as a legitimate complaint this clinic can help with (e.g. physiotherapy, osteopathy, or acupuncture are all reasonable fits for a whole-body/systemic presentation) and either asks one plain-language clarifying question or proceeds with its own judgement -- it must not say this is out of scope or that the clinic doesn't treat it, and must not call any tool this turn without first reasoning about the complaint.

scenarios.name: Confident single fit needs no clarifying question and fires the needle check

history.content: I've been feeling really run down, exhausted, and I can't sleep properly -- I was wondering if acupuncture might help with that

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent lands on Chinese Medicine & Acupuncture (the caller already named it, and fatigue/sleep issues don't have a genuinely competing structural-vs-rehab modality at this clinic) and, since acupuncture is now the plan, asks the needle-comfort check as this turn's only spoken output ('acupuncture does involve needles...are you okay with that?' or equivalent). FAIL if the agent asks an unrelated hands-on-vs-rehab clarifying question, skips the needle check entirely, or calls a tool before the needle check has been asked and answered.

scenarios.name: Caller explicitly defers the choice -- no clarifying question, agent decides

history.content: My knee's been sore since I started running again a few weeks ago -- honestly not sure what I need, whatever you think is best

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent does NOT ask a hands-on-vs-rehab (or any other) clarifying question -- since the caller explicitly deferred, the agent should make the category call itself using its own judgement and move on (e.g. proceed toward the timeframe question, or straight to the tool call if timeframe is already known). FAIL if the agent asks the caller to choose between two approaches after they've already said 'whatever you think is best'.

scenarios.name: Caller pivots to cancel during intake — routes to cancel_intent with a filler phrase

history.content: My knee has been bothering me after my run last week
Oh, that's not ideal — you've come to the right place. Are you after something more hands-on, or more of a rehab and strengthening focus?
Actually, never mind — can I cancel my appointment instead?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks one filler phrase from the TOOL-CALL FILLER set AND calls universal_router intent='cancel_intent', in the same turn (per the ESCAPE ROUTE OUTPUT FORMAT). FAIL if agent continues the intake flow, asks a qualifying question before routing, omits the filler phrase, or speaks anything beyond the single filler phrase.

scenarios.name: Plain pricing question during intake routes to PRICING QUERY, not INFO PIVOT

history.content: I've been getting really bad lower back pain, it's been going on for about two months

Oh, that's not ideal — you've come to the right place. Are you after something more hands-on — joint work and manual therapy to get things moving and reduce the pain directly? Or more of a rehab and exercise focus, understanding what's causing it and building strength so it doesn't keep coming back?
Actually, before I decide — how much does a physio session cost?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks one filler phrase from the TOOL-CALL FILLER set and calls universal_router intent='get_service_price' (the system prompt's PRICING QUERY path — stays in this node, does not eject to info_pivot). FAIL if agent calls universal_router intent='info_pivot' for a plain, uncombined pricing question.

scenarios.name: Combined price+duration question still routes to INFO PIVOT (regression guard)

history.content: How much does a physio session cost and how long does it run?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks one filler phrase and calls universal_router intent='info_pivot' (system prompt's COMBINED ASK SCOPED EXCEPTION routes same-turn price+duration asks to info_pivot/Node 8). FAIL if agent calls get_service_price directly for this combined ask, or fails to call any tool.

scenarios.name: Caller only wants to check an existing appointment — routes to details, not cancel_intent

history.content: Hi, can you just check what time my appointment is for on Thursday?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent says "Checking that now, one moment." and calls universal_router intent='details' (system prompt's PATIENT APPOINTMENT LOOKUP, PHASE A). FAIL if agent calls universal_router intent='cancel_intent' for a pure check/confirm request with no cancel or reschedule language.

scenarios.name: Genuine cancel request still routes to cancel_intent (regression guard)

history.content: I've been getting shoulder pain from gardening
Oh, that's not ideal — you've come to the right place. Are you after something more hands-on, or more of a rehab and strengthening focus?
Actually, forget it — I need to cancel my appointment for Friday instead

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks one filler phrase then calls universal_router intent='cancel_intent'. FAIL if agent routes to intent='details' or continues the complaint-intake flow instead of escaping.

scenarios.name: STEP 6 presents due-rank order as returned — no more focus-match reorder

history.content: I hurt my knee playing tennis a couple of weeks ago
Oh, that's not ideal — you've come to the right place. Are you after something more hands-on, or more of a rehab and exercise focus?
Definitely the rehab and exercise side, I want to build it back up properly
Do you have a preference for seeing a male or female practitioner, or no preference?
No preference. I'd like to come in this week if possible.
Let me just have a look here for you.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent's next turn presents Alex Donald (due_rank 1, first entry in the tool result) with his 9:00 AM Wednesday slot, plus a clinical justification connecting physiotherapy to a knee injury, and a closing question. FAIL if the agent presents Mia Navratil or Parinaz Kheirandish instead of Alex Donald -- there is no reorder step anymore, so the first-ranked entry in the tool result must be what's offered first.

scenarios.name: Who's-best query presents the top due-rank candidate directly, no specialty exclusion

history.content: Who's best for general deconditioning after being sick for a few weeks?
Let me just have a look here for you.

TOOL RESULT (smart_voice_agent, intent=recommend_availability): {"success": true, "session_id": "sess_test2", "recommendations": [{"practitioner_id": "p_scott", "practitioner_name": "Scott Lyon", "appointment_type_id": "at_pilates_initial", "appointment_type": "Clinical Pilates Initial", "due_rank": 1, "available_slots": [{"date": "2026-09-16", "day_of_week": "Wednesday", "slot_groups": {"morning": ["8:00 AM"]}}], "earliest_slot": {"date": "2026-09-16", "time": "8:00 AM"}}, {"practitioner_id": "p_jordan", "practitioner_name": "Jordan Suen", "appointment_type_id": "at_chiro_initial", "appointment_type": "Chiropractic Initial", "due_rank": 2, "available_slots": [{"date": "2026-09-17", "day_of_week": "Thursday", "slot_groups": {"afternoon": ["1:00 PM"]}}], "earliest_slot": {"date": "2026-09-17", "time": "1:00 PM"}}], "first_available": {"practitioner_id": "p_scott", "practitioner_name": "Scott Lyon", "date": "2026-09-16", "time": "8:00 AM"}}

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent presents Scott Lyon (due_rank 1) with his 8:00 AM Wednesday slot, a real clinical justification connecting Clinical Pilates to general deconditioning, and a closing question -- there is no practitioner-specialty exclusion data anymore, so the top due-rank entry is simply presented. FAIL if the agent says there is no availability, refuses to answer the who's-best question, or presents Jordan Suen instead of Scott Lyon when Scott Lyon has bookable slots.

scenarios.name: Straightforward back pain (with a stated mechanism) gets a modality explanation, never a soon/timeframe question

history.content: I twisted my back badly lifting something at work yesterday

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent's response does not ask any timeframe or urgency question (no 'when would you like to come in', 'are you looking to get in soon, or do you have a timeframe in mind', or equivalent), does not ask a clarifying question either (a stated lifting mechanism is a STEP 1 SKIP CONDITION -- it lands on Physiotherapy without asking), and instead speaks a short, complaint-specific reason connecting physiotherapy to a recent lifting injury, then moves straight toward checking availability (a bridge line and/or the recommend_availability tool call) in the same turn with no question in between. FAIL if the agent asks a hands-on-vs-rehab clarifying question, asks a standalone timeframe/soon question, or gives no complaint-specific explanation at all for its modality choice.

scenarios.name: Bare complaint with no duration/history signal asks the PRIMARY clarifying question (STEP 1 concrete-signal rewrite)

history.content: my back hurts

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent's only spoken output this turn is a single combined question asking both how long the complaint has been going on AND whether the caller has tried physio, chiro, or osteo for it before (the PRIMARY QUESTION) -- no tool call, no other question this turn. FAIL if the agent skips straight to a modality recommendation or availability check with no clarifying question, asks a hands-on-vs-rehab FALLBACK-style question instead of the duration/history PRIMARY question, or asks more than one question this turn.

scenarios.name: PRIMARY QUESTION answer resolves the category via prior treatment history

history.content: my back hurts
How long has this been going on, and have you tried anything like physio, chiro, or osteo for it before?
It's been on and off for months, and chiro really helped last time

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent lands on Chiropractic (resolved by the caller's own prior-treatment answer) without asking a second FALLBACK clarifying question, speaks a short complaint-specific reason connecting chiropractic to the caller's chronic back pain, and moves toward checking availability. FAIL if the agent asks a further hands-on-vs-rehab question after this answer already resolved it, or ignores the stated prior treatment and lands on a different category with no justification.

scenarios.name: PRIMARY QUESTION answer doesn't resolve it -- FALLBACK QUESTION fires next, generalised wording

history.content: my back hurts
How long has this been going on, and have you tried anything like physio, chiro, or osteo for it before?
Just started yesterday, haven't tried anything yet

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent asks the FALLBACK QUESTION -- a plain-language question naming the live candidate categories (e.g. hands-on/manual work vs. rehab-and-exercise, optionally folding in acupuncture) without reciting clinical modality names as a multiple-choice menu -- as its only spoken output this turn, since an acute complaint with nothing tried before doesn't resolve the category from the PRIMARY answer alone. FAIL if the agent skips straight to a modality recommendation without asking FALLBACK, or asks a third/different question.

scenarios.name: Red-flag symptom triggers safety escalation, not routine triage (new ESCAPE ROUTE 1)

history.content: I've had this weird numbness down my leg and I've actually been losing control of my bladder the last few days

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent's only spoken output this turn is the safety escalation message directing the caller to see a GP urgently or go to the emergency department, with no tool call and no continuation of the normal complaint-intake/triage flow. FAIL if the agent asks a clarifying question, proceeds toward booking or availability, or fails to mention urgent care.

scenarios.name: Ordinary back pain does not trigger safety escalation (false-positive regression guard)

history.content: my back's been absolutely killing me the last few days

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent does NOT give the safety escalation message -- 'killing me' here is ordinary pain language, not a genuine red-flag symptom (no numbness/weakness, chest pain, bladder/bowel loss, weight loss, fever, or major trauma stated) -- and instead proceeds with normal STEP 1 triage (asking the PRIMARY clarifying question, since no duration/history signal was given). FAIL if the agent escalates this as a safety concern.

scenarios.name: Red flag surfaces mid-conversation, after STEP 1 has already started

history.content: my back hurts
How long has this been going on, and have you tried anything like physio, chiro, or osteo for it before?
A few months now, but actually the last couple of days I've noticed I can't really feel my right leg properly

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent's next turn is the safety escalation message (SAFETY ESCALATION ESCAPE ROUTE) rather than continuing the PRIMARY/FALLBACK question flow or moving toward booking -- the escape route is checked every turn, so a red flag volunteered mid-conversation must still divert. FAIL if the agent continues normal triage, ignores the numbness, or proceeds to a modality recommendation.

scenarios.name: After answering the clarifying question, agent explains the modality (not a timeframe question) before checking availability

history.content: I've been getting really bad lower back pain, it's been going on for about two months

Oh, that's not ideal — you've come to the right place. Are you after something more hands-on — joint work and manual therapy to get things moving and reduce the pain directly? Or more of a rehab and exercise focus, understanding what's causing it and building strength so it doesn't keep coming back?
Definitely the hands-on side

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent's next turn speaks a short, complaint-specific reason connecting the chosen category (e.g. chiropractic or osteopathy) to the caller's back pain, and does NOT ask a standalone timeframe question ('when would you like to come in', 'are you looking to get in soon...'). It may continue straight into a bridge line before checking availability. FAIL if the agent asks a timeframe question instead of, or in addition to, explaining the modality choice, or gives no modality explanation at all this turn.

scenarios.name: Named practitioner with nothing available widens into their own modality (STEP 7 STAGE 2 fallback)

history.content: Can I book in with Angelo? My back's been really tight.
Let me check what Angelo has available for you.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent does not error or get stuck -- since Angelo Marketos's only entry (approach 'A', a single practitioner) has nothing available, STEP 7 STAGE 1 must fall straight through (there is no second array entry to advance to) into STAGE 2, which should widen into Angelo's own modality (Chiropractic, per PRACTITIONER LOOKUP) with a spoken transition line, and call smart_voice_agent again with categories instead of practitioners. FAIL if the agent tries to read a second entry from an empty/single-item array, stalls with no further tool call or spoken output, or asks the caller a question unrelated to widening the search.
